userStories.title: Implement outbound WebSocket transport with auth-host handshake and backoff reconnect
userStories.description: As share.ts, I need a transport that connects to the relay wsUrl, sends the auth-host envelope as its first frame, exposes a send() method, surfaces inbound frames via a callback, and reconnects on drop with exponential backoff.
acceptanceCriteria: Working dir: /Users/tuongaz/dev/seeflow/apps/studio
Create src/share-transport.ts exporting interface ShareTransport { send(frame: Envelope): void; close(reason?: string): void; isOpen(): boolean }

Export createShareTransport(opts: { wsUrl: string; sessionId: string; hostKey: string; onFrame: (env: Envelope) => void; onStateChange: (s: 'connecting' | 'open' | 'reconnecting' | 'closed') => void; wsFactory?: (url: string) => WebSocketLike }): ShareTransport
WebSocketLike is a minimal interface { addEventListener; removeEventListener; send; close; readyState } so tests can inject a fake; default factory uses Bun's global WebSocket
On open, transport immediately sends one frame: makeEnvelope('auth-host', { sessionId, hostKey }, { from: 'host' })
Inbound text frames are JSON.parsed then parseEnvelope'd; valid frames invoke onFrame; invalid frames are dropped and a console.warn logs `{ reason }` (never the payload)
On close (code !== 1000) or error, transport waits backoff then reconnects: initial 500ms, doubles to a 30000ms cap, with +/- 20 percent jitter
close('user') sets a stopped flag that suppresses further reconnect attempts
send() throws if isOpen() is false; callers must check first

Create src/share-transport.test.ts using an in-memory FakeWebSocket; cover: auth-host sent as first frame after open, onFrame invoked for valid frame, invalid frame dropped without invoking onFrame, reconnect on unexpected close attempts a new wsFactory call after backoff (use mock timers — Bun supports `setSystemTime`/`useFakeTimers` or hand-rolled clock injection), close('user') prevents reconnect
`bun test src/share-transport.test.ts` passes (>=5 cases)

userStories.title: Implement stop(), kick(), and rotateUrl() lifecycle methods
userStories.description: As the local API, I need stop() to tear the session down cleanly, kick() to send a kick envelope to a specific peer, and rotateUrl() to stop+restart with a fresh token so an abused link can be invalidated.
acceptanceCriteria: Working dir: /Users/tuongaz/dev/seeflow/apps/studio
Modify src/share.ts:
stop() while state.status === 'active': transitions to { status: 'stopping' }, calls transport.close('user'), clears in-memory hostKey/token, transitions to { status: 'idle' }, resolves
stop() while state.status === 'idle': resolves as a no-op (does not throw)
stop() while state.status === 'starting': aborts the start() promise with Error('share-stopped-during-start'), then completes the stopping flow

kick(peerId): rejects with Error('share-not-active') if state.status !== 'active'; else looks up the peer's connId via internal peer map (added in US-019 — for this story require state.peers entry to carry peerId and use peerId as the `to` value, peer→connId mapping deferred to router story) and sends transport.send(makeEnvelope('kick', { peerId }, { to: peerId }))

rotateUrl(): rejects if state.status !== 'active'; otherwise calls stop() then start() and returns the new { url } — host's previously printed URL/token is now invalid because relay row was deleted by stop (note: relay-side delete is a future story — for now rotateUrl simply mints a new session and abandons the old one)

Extend src/share.test.ts: (a) stop from active reaches idle and clears state, (b) stop from idle is a no-op, (c) stop during starting rejects the original start, (d) kick from idle rejects with share-not-active, (e) kick from active calls transport.send with a kick envelope addressed to peerId, (f) rotateUrl from active returns a new url and the old token is no longer in state

userStories.title: Implement incoming-frame router with presence handling and peer tracking
userStories.description: As share.ts, every inbound envelope must be Zod-validated, dispatched by type, and presence frames must update state.peers so kick() and the UI can address peers by id. RPC dispatch into operations.ts is out of scope (phase 4); router for v1 only handles presence, rpc-result echo, and drops everything else with a structured log.
acceptanceCriteria: Working dir: /Users/tuongaz/dev/seeflow/apps/studio
Add an internal handleFrame(env: Envelope) function in src/share.ts invoked from the transport's onFrame callback
handleFrame branches by env.type:
'presence' with payload { kind: 'join'; peerId; displayName }: append to state.peers (dedup by peerId), transition state, store an internal Map<peerId, connId> using env.from
'presence' with payload { kind: 'leave'; peerId }: remove from state.peers and the connId map
'presence' with payload { kind: 'cursor' | 'viewport' | other }: forward to subscribers as a sideband event (no state.peers change) — for v1 just no-op, just don't reject

'rpc' / 'file-request' / 'file-upload-intent' / 'file-upload-done' / 'sse' / 'node-patched' / 'files-manifest' / 'rpc-result' / 'kick' / 'file-bytes' / 'file-redirect': v1 logs `{ type, from }` and drops (real handling lands in phase 4+)
Unknown frame (parseEnvelope failure): already logged in transport, never reaches handleFrame
kick(peerId) (from US-018) now consults the internal Map<peerId, connId> and addresses the frame to that connId; if peerId is unknown, kick rejects with Error('share-peer-not-found')
Use a Zod sub-schema for the presence payload so malformed presence frames are dropped without crashing

Create integration/share-host-peer.it.ts (bun-test, picked up by `bun run test:it:bun` per the existing integration test glob)

Implement an in-process FakeRelay: (a) a Bun.serve listening on 127.0.0.1:0 that exposes POST /api/share/sessions returning { sessionId, token, hostKey, wsUrl: 'ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/' }, (b) a Bun.serve WebSocket on the same port that accepts both host and stubbed-peer connections, validates the auth-host frame against the issued hostKey, and routes envelopes by `to` field exactly like the real relay's ws-default.ts

Test 1 (start handshake): start the FakeRelay, build a studio app via createApi with the share controller pointed at FakeRelay's URL, POST /api/share/start, assert the response contains url+sessionId, assert FakeRelay observed exactly one host WS connection that sent auth-host { sessionId, hostKey } as its first frame

All four tests use real Bun WebSocket on both ends (no mocks at the network boundary) so transport/auth/router get genuine round-trip coverage
Each FakeRelay instance picks a free port (port:0) and is fully torn down in afterAll/afterEach so the test file is hermetic and parallel-safe
